text: Windows diagnosis at ff295e5dd21071373be709928e084a4ddef570fd: test_workspace_agent_process_parser is not recursively overflowing its stack. In test_invalid_configuration_fails_closed, excessive.windows_bindings.assign(max+1, excessive.windows_bindings.front()) passes a reference to an element of the same vector. MSVC Debug deterministically stops after the invalid-configuration marker with vector:1352, assignment value cannot be a reference into the container. In Release, vector::assign reallocates/frees the old storage before fill reads the referenced value, producing allocator/layout-sensitive use-after-invalidation; Windows may surface this as fail-fast 0xc0000409 (STATUS_STACK_BUFFER_OVERRUN), whereas a true stack overflow is 0xc00000fd. Exact Release binary passed 500/500 locally and the ff295e5dd hosted diagnostic run 32713056293 passed once, confirming nondeterminism. Action: copy front() to a standalone WorkspaceAgentWindowsProcessParserBinding before assign; likewise copying before adjacent push_back is prudent. No product/test code changed in this diagnostic.
